title: Sign-in, Copilot connection errors and the agent core
owns: app/main/agent/** (presenter.ts: friendlyError only), app/main/agent/auth.ts, sign-in handling in main.ts, the build-time client id (scripts/build-app.mjs), the README's sign-in requirement paragraph, the home window's Copilot section strings

findings.title: "Sign in with GitHub" cannot sign anyone in on a release build; the real path needs the GitHub CLI, which nothing tells the user to install
findings.scenario: A non-technical user installs Ember on Windows or macOS (no gh, no terminal habit), agrees, presses Start and gets "Not connected to Copilot: sign in with GitHub below." Pressing the button gives "In a terminal, run “gh auth login”. Ember will notice…" with a Cancel button. The device flow is dead code because process.env.EMBER_GITHUB_CLIENT_ID is read at runtime and nothing sets it (no build-time define; PLAN.md §7 Q1 'Open'). Nothing says gh must be installed, and ghCliToken() returns null both for 'gh missing' and 'not logged in', so Check again says only "No GitHub sign-in found… Run gh auth login". The README has no sign-in step and never says a GitHub account with Copilot is needed (grep for sign in/subscription/account/gh auth in README.md finds nothing relevant). The doctor's fix, "choose Sign in with GitHub, or run gh auth login", has the same gap. Only docs/DEVELOPING.md §'Connecting Copilot' explains it. Result: on a clean machine, first run ends at a dead end.
findings.evidence: app/main/main.ts:964-981 (clientId check, 'waiting' message); app/main/agent/auth.ts:7; app/renderer/home/copy.ts:55; app/main/doctor.ts (copilot row fix); grep -rn EMBER_GITHUB_CLIENT_ID scripts packaging app finds only these reads; grep README.md finds no 'gh auth', 'GitHub CLI' or Copilot-subscription text; no user-facing 'install the GitHub CLI' string anywhere under app/. Rendered the macOS after-Start window: after the click only the Cancel button and the terminal instruction show.
findings.fix: Preferred: register Ember's GitHub App and bake the client id into the build, so the device flow runs. If it must ship without that: (1) README 'Before you start' step: a GitHub account with Copilot, plus the GitHub CLI with per-OS commands (winget install GitHub.cli / brew install gh / sudo dnf install gh) and `gh auth login`. (2) Detect a missing gh (which/ghCliPath) and say "GitHub CLI isn't installed" with the install command or link in the Copilot section. (3) Relabel the button "Connect with GitHub CLI" so it doesn't promise a browser sign-in. (4) Make the doctor row say the same.

findings.title: A fresh Windows or macOS user cannot sign in: no OAuth client id ships, and nothing says the GitHub CLI must be installed
findings.scenario: Someone downloads Ember on a clean PC, agrees to the consent card and clicks "Sign in with GitHub". `EMBER_GITHUB_CLIENT_ID` is read only from the process environment, so the device flow is skipped. Ember shows "In a terminal, run `gh auth login`" and waits 10 minutes (200 polls, 3 s apart). They do not have `gh`, and neither the bubble, the settings text nor the README's Windows and macOS install sections say to install it or where to get it. They can never connect. (PLAN §7 open question 1 still lists registering Ember's GitHub App as open.)
findings.evidence: `grep -rn EMBER_GITHUB_CLIENT_ID` finds it only in main.ts:964 and PLAN/auth.ts comments. scripts/build-app.mjs has no `define` and there is nothing in packaging/ or scripts/ that sets it. The only in-app copy is main.ts:967 and app/renderer/home/copy.ts:55 ("No GitHub sign-in found on this computer. Run “gh auth login” in a terminal..."). README.md's Install on Windows and Install on macOS sections have no sign-in step. docs/DEVELOPING.md says `sudo dnf install gh`, which is Linux-only.
findings.fix: Register the GitHub App and bake the client id into the build (an esbuild `define` or a packaged constant) before release. If the release has to ship without it, make every sign-in message and the README name the requirement: "Install the GitHub CLI from cli.github.com, run gh auth login, then press Check again", with an Open page button. Do not label the button "Sign in with GitHub" when it only waits for `gh`.

findings.title: A packaged Ember can only sign in through the GitHub CLI, and the install docs never say so
findings.platforms: all (worst on Windows and macOS, where gh is not normally installed)
findings.scenario: A person installs the RPM, zip or dmg exactly as README.md says and presses "Sign in with GitHub" in the first-run window. Ember's own GitHub App is not registered (PLAN.md §7 item 1 is still "Open"), and the device flow only runs when the environment variable EMBER_GITHUB_CLIENT_ID is set, which a Start-menu or Finder launch will not have. So the button only shows "In a terminal, run 'gh auth login'...". Without the GitHub CLI installed, nothing in the window or in README.md tells them to install it, and no other sign-in path exists. The result is a running Ember that can never connect to Copilot. The doctor's Copilot row gives the same advice.
findings.evidence: main.ts:964-972 reads process.env.EMBER_GITHUB_CLIENT_ID. It is not gated by devEnv, but no packaged build supplies one. When it is unset, the only message is "In a terminal, run “gh auth login”..." (also app/renderer/home/copy.ts:55 and app/main/doctor.ts:168). `grep -n -i "gh auth\|GitHub CLI\|sign in" README.md` finds no sign-in guidance in the Linux, Windows or macOS install sections. The gh requirement appears only in docs/DEVELOPING.md:191-205. PLAN.md:389: "Who registers Ember's GitHub App? Open".
findings.fix: Before release, register the GitHub App and bake its (public) client id into the build, for example from package.json or an esbuild define, keeping the env var as an override. If the release has to ship without it, put a "Sign in needs the GitHub CLI: install it from cli.github.com, run gh auth login" step in each README install section. Make the sign-in window say it, with a link, when gh is not found.

findings.title: "Sign in with GitHub" is a dead end: it only says to run gh auth login, and the README never mentions Copilot or the GitHub CLI
findings.scenario: A new user on a packaged build (EMBER_GITHUB_CLIENT_ID is unset) opens Settings, sees "Not connected to Copilot: sign in with GitHub below.", presses Sign in with GitHub, and gets "In a terminal, run “gh auth login”…". Nothing says the GitHub CLI must be installed first (Windows and macOS don't ship it), and "Check again" repeats "Run gh auth login". README.md has no get-started or sign-in section: its only sign-in mentions are about uninstalling and the SSH note.
findings.evidence: Ran the real app under xvfb with GH_TOKEN, GITHUB_TOKEN and EMBER_GITHUB_CLIENT_ID unset and gh off PATH. The Copilot section showed that agent line and button, and after the click "In a terminal, run “gh auth login”. Ember will notice within a few seconds and connect; no restart needed." (screenshot shots/signin.png under the scratch folder). Check again gave copy.ts:55 "No GitHub sign-in found on this computer. Run “gh auth login” in a terminal…". grep finds EMBER_GITHUB_CLIENT_ID only in auth.ts, main.ts and PLAN.md §7 (open question 1: the GitHub App is not registered). The gh-CLI route is documented only in docs/DEVELOPING.md.
findings.fix: Short term, make the words honest: label the button "Connect with GitHub CLI", or have the message say "Install the GitHub CLI (cli.github.com), then run “gh auth login” in a terminal", and give copy.ts:55 the same sentence. Add a "First run" section to README.md saying you need a GitHub account with Copilot and, until Ember's app is registered, the GitHub CLI signed in (or GH_TOKEN). Better: register the app and bake the client id into packaged builds.

findings.title: Transient errors while connecting (GitHub 5xx/429, a slow response, the SDK's 30 s start timeout) are shown as raw SDK text and never retried
findings.scenario: Ember starts at login while GitHub has a blip, or while the machine is still waking or the VPN is settling. `client.listModels()` or `getAuthStatus()` fails with something like "Request models.list failed with message: 503 Service Unavailable". Ember goes to the error phase (handle: "Copilot problem"; settings show the raw text) and stays there. Asking a question does not reconnect it either. Only an offline error gets the 15 s / 30 s / 60 s retry and the retry-on-ask. The user has to open settings and press Check again. On a slow first launch, "Timeout waiting for CLI server to start" behaves the same way.
findings.evidence: Ran AgentHost against a fake SDK whose listModels throws each of three messages. Every run gave `{"phase":"error","reason":"other","detail":"Request models.list failed with message: 503 Service Unavailable","retryScheduled":false}`. The 429 and "Request timed out after 30000ms" messages gave the same result. The "Request <rpc> failed with message: …" shape is what the real runtime produces (seen live: "Request models.list failed with message: Not authenticated…"). `offline = online === false || unreachable || NETWORK.test(err)` (host.ts:1076) and NETWORK has no 5xx, 429 or generic timeout. startErrorReason and explainStartError have no case for them, so they fall through to `other` / the raw message (host.ts:291-348). `ask()` only calls retryNow() when a retry is already scheduled (host.ts:1337).
findings.fix: Treat 5xx, 429, "timed out", "Timeout waiting for CLI server" and SessionToolsTimeoutError as transient: retryLater() with the existing backoff, run the same retry-on-ask, and map them to a sentence ("Copilot had a problem on its side; I'll try again") instead of the raw RPC text. Reuse friendlyError's 5xx/429 patterns.

findings.title: After a mid-session token rejection Ember still says Ready, settings offer only "Sign out", and GitHub App tokens that expire are never refreshed
findings.scenario: The user's token is revoked, or the Copilot seat is removed, or a GitHub-App `ghu_` token passes its 8-hour life. The next question shows "Copilot didn't accept the sign-in. Open settings to sign in again." The bubble has no Open settings button. The agent phase never leaves "ready", so the handle still says "Ready". Settings show "Signed in as <login>" with only a Sign out button, because "Sign in with GitHub" and "Check again" are hidden unless the phase is signed-out or error. Every later question fails the same way. The only way out is to guess Sign out and then sign in again, which for a gh/env token also means `gh auth login`.
findings.evidence: Real runtime, mock endpoint answering 401 (BYOK, so the wording differs): after the turn `phase=ready`, and a second question gave the same error with `phase=ready`. Nothing in host.ts or conductor.ts reacts to a session.error, so the phase never changes. The bubble for session.error is built with `actions: []` (presenter.ts:773-786), unlike fail() and notice(). renderAgent gates the buttons with `notConnected = phase === "signed-out" || phase === "error"` (renderer/home/main.ts:460-468). pollDeviceFlow returns only `access_token` (auth.ts:153), dropping `refresh_token` and `expires_in`. isUsableToken accepts `ghu_`, the GitHub-App token prefix that expires after 8 hours when the app uses the default expiring user tokens. The SDK offers gitHubTokenProvider for refresh, and Ember does not use it.
findings.fix: On a session.error with errorType authentication, or a 401/403, from the conductor or a task, have the host call getAuthStatus(). If it is not authenticated, set phase "error" with reason "sign-in" so settings show Sign in and Check again and the handle says "Sign-in refused". Add Open settings to that bubble. Store the refresh token and expiry from the device flow and use gitHubTokenProvider (or refresh before expiry), or register the GitHub App with expiring user tokens turned off.

findings.title: A rejected GITHUB_TOKEN/GH_TOKEN/COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN silently shadows a working `gh auth login`, and the error's advice cannot fix it
findings.scenario: A developer has `GITHUB_TOKEN` or `GH_TOKEN` set to a fine-grained PAT without the Copilot permission, a token for another account, or one gone stale. They are also logged in with `gh` and expect Ember to use that. `resolveToken` returns the environment token first. Ember tries it three times and then says "Copilot didn't accept the GitHub sign-in Ember found (a token from the environment)… Sign in again, or run gh auth login in a terminal and press Check again." Check again picks the same environment token. "Sign in with GitHub" waits for a token different from the current one and finds none for 10 minutes. The message does not say which variable it was. The user has to work out that an environment variable must be unset and Ember restarted.
findings.evidence: `resolveToken(null, {GITHUB_TOKEN:'github_pat_…'}, async () => 'gho_…')` returns `{source:'environment'}` and never reaches gh. doStart (host.ts:762-793) throws after three refused tries and has no fallback to the next source. retrySignIn (main.ts:945) and the sign-in watch loop (main.ts:970, compares `found.token !== before`) both call the same resolveToken. The explainStartError text is host.ts:345.
findings.fix: When a token from the environment or gh is refused, try the next source before giving up (record which sources failed), and name the variable in the message ("GITHUB_TOKEN was refused; unset it or press Check again to use your gh sign-in"). Have Check again skip a source that was just refused.

findings.title: The device-flow sign-in dies on one network blip or proxy error page, and promises a retry that does not exist
findings.platforms: all (live once a client id ships)
findings.scenario: The user has entered the code on github.com. While Ember polls (up to 15 minutes), one fetch fails (Wi-Fi roam, VPN reconnect) or a proxy returns an HTML 502. The whole sign-in aborts. A network error says "Ember can't reach GitHub right now. It will try again when the network is back", but nothing retries a sign-in (only starts are retried). An HTML 502 shows the raw "Unexpected token '<', "<html>…" is not valid JSON". The code the user just approved is lost, and they must start over.
findings.evidence: Scratch run of pollDeviceFlow. A `fetch failed` on the second poll threw TypeError: fetch failed, and the user text was "Ember can't reach GitHub right now. It will try again when the network is back." A 502 whose body is not JSON threw SyntaxError, and the user text was the raw "Unexpected token '<'…". The `await fetch(...)` and `res.json()` at auth.ts:147-152 are not guarded, and main.ts:936-941 maps the error through explainStartError, which has the "will try again" sentence.
findings.fix: In the poll loop, catch network errors, non-JSON bodies and 5xx responses, wait one interval and keep polling until the code expires or the user cancels. Give signInError its own text ("Lost the connection to GitHub; your code is still valid, I'll keep waiting").

findings.title: Any ENOENT/EACCES during start or sign-in is reported as "Ember's Copilot runtime is missing… Reinstall Ember"; a failed token-file write throws away a completed sign-in
findings.scenario: The user finishes the device-flow approval, but writing github-token.bin fails (read-only or full profile, a deleted userData folder, antivirus). `TokenStore.save` guards only `encryptString`, so `writeFileSync` throws and the whole sign-in ends with "Ember's Copilot runtime is missing or can't start. Reinstall Ember (sudo dnf reinstall ember)." Reinstalling cannot help, and the token would have worked for this run. The same wrong sentence appears for any file error in the start path (mkdir of the work folder, agent.json).
findings.evidence: Scratch run: `new TokenStore('/tmp/…/nope/github-token.bin', box).save(token)` threw ENOENT, and explainStartError(e) returned the runtime-missing text. The pattern is `/not found at|ENOENT|EACCES|spawn /i` at host.ts:337, and startErrorReason at host.ts:293 maps it to reason "runtime".
findings.fix: Wrap the write in try/catch and return false, which the sign-in flow already handles ("you'll need to sign in again next time"). In explainStartError, name the runtime as missing only for `spawn` errors or errors mentioning the runtime path, and give other ENOENT/EACCES/EPERM/EBUSY/ENOSPC errors their own sentence naming the file.

findings.title: A "show me" guide queues silently behind two long tasks while the model is told it started
findings.scenario: Two tasks are running (each can take up to 20 minutes). The user asks "show me how to turn on Night Light". The guide counts against `maxRunning = 2`, so it waits. show_me still returns "Guide N started: Ember will point at each step… Tell the user to follow Ember", so Ember says "Follow my pointer" while nothing is pointing. The card says only "Waiting to start".
findings.evidence: TaskManager scratch run with two never-ending running tasks and a third `start(…, {mode:"guide"})` gave `guide status: queued` and cards `…=running/Working…, …=running/Working…, show me how…=waiting/Waiting to start`. The host's reply is built unconditionally at host.ts:1038-1040.
findings.fix: Don't count guides toward maxRunning (they act on nothing), or run them ahead of queued tasks. Failing that, have show_me say "queued behind N running tasks" when `status === "queued"`.

findings.title: `gh auth token` is asked without `--hostname github.com`, so GH_HOST or an enterprise-only login yields a token Copilot can't use
findings.scenario: A developer at a company with GitHub Enterprise Server has GH_HOST set, or is logged in only to the enterprise host. `gh auth token` prints that host's token. Ember sends it to Copilot on github.com, which refuses it. The error says the sign-in "may have expired", which is misleading, and Check again cannot help.
findings.evidence: ghCliToken runs `execFile(gh, ["auth","token"], …)` with no host argument. `gh auth token` uses GH_HOST or the default host. By its documented behaviour `--hostname` is the way to choose; I could not run gh here.
findings.fix: Run `gh auth token --hostname github.com` (add `--user` handling if needed), and fall through when that host has no login.

findings.title: Default models are picked by list order and name only, never by cost: the worker is the first non-"mini" vision model listed
findings.scenario: Copilot lists models in whatever order its API returns. A premium model with a high billing multiplier can come before a standard one. Every task step (with screenshots) then runs on it, burning quota or AI credits at several times the rate, and the user only learns when the usage limit message ("Try again a bit later") appears. The conductor can similarly land on a code-tuned or slow reasoning "mini" model such as `grok-code-fast-1` or `o4-mini` (the FAST regex matches them).
findings.evidence: chooseModels: `worker = vision.find(m => !FAST.some(...)) ?? vision[0]` and `usable.find(FAST…) ?? usable[0]`. The SDK's ModelInfo carries `billing.multiplier` and `billing.tokenPrices`, and PLAN.md:72 says billing is usage-based, but nothing in app/ reads them. The real list order could not be checked offline.
findings.fix: Rank candidates by `billing.multiplier` (or token price) as well, prefer ≤1×, and skip names that mark coding-only or reasoning models for the conductor. Show the chosen models and their cost class in settings.

findings.title: A throwing makeWorker leaves the task "waiting" for ever, Stop does nothing, and the rejection is unhandled
findings.scenario: If anything in the host's makeWorker throws (building hands, a targets-runtime call, the Worker constructor), run() rejects before its try block. The card stays "Waiting to start" with a Stop button that does nothing, because the task is neither queued nor running. It occupies the card list until Ember restarts, and the error is only an unhandled-rejection log line. I found no realistic trigger today (handsFor is itself guarded), so this is hardening.
findings.evidence: Scratch run with `makeWorker: () => { throw new Error('boom') }`: `UNHANDLED REJECTION: Error: boom`, status after 200 ms `queued`, still `queued` after cancel(). `const worker = this.d.makeWorker(...)` is outside the try in run() (tasks.ts:238), and pump() discards the promise with `void run.finally(...)` (tasks.ts:230-232).
findings.fix: Move makeWorker inside the try, so a throw becomes a failed task with friendlyError text, or catch in pump() and call finish(task, "failed", …).

findings.title: The worker's identity says it never moves the user's mouse or types on their keyboard, but press_keys, scroll and cursor clicks do exactly that (after asking)
findings.scenario: The prompt tells the model: "They operate applications through the accessibility system, without moving the user's mouse or typing on their keyboard." The same session is given press_keys ("Borrows the user's keyboard, so the user is asked first"), scroll, and type_text/click that escalate to the borrowed mouse. A model that believes its identity may avoid those tools and give up early, or tell the user "I won't touch your mouse" just before Ember asks to borrow it.
findings.evidence: worker-persona.ts:18 (OPERATES, used for every local-screen worker) against worker.ts:1156 and the router escalation in act() (worker.ts:1863-1865). Prompt/tool name cross-check across 12 worker configurations and 6 conductor configurations found no tool named but not offered, apart from the conductor prompt naming list_tasks, cancel_task and steer_task when the host has no TaskManager.
findings.fix: Reword to "They use the accessibility system first; only when an app needs it, they may borrow the user's mouse or keyboard, and the user is always asked first."

findings.title: Docs and a code comment say a failed task card stays until closed, but it disappears after 60 s
findings.scenario: DEVELOPING.md tells users "a failed card stays until you close it", and main.ts says failure cards stay until a click closes them and so Stop everything also clears them. A user (or screen-reader user) who steps away for two minutes comes back to no card and no sign of the failure outside the settings Conversation. The unit test asserts the 60 s auto-close, so the docs and comment are stale.
findings.evidence: tasks.ts:283 `status === "failed" ? failureCardMs ?? 60_000 : cardMs ?? 15_000`; test/unit/tasks.test.ts:472 ("a failed card goes on its own after the longer failure time"); docs/DEVELOPING.md:131; main.ts:805.
findings.fix: Either keep failed cards until closed, as documented (pass a very large failureCardMs), or correct the docs and comment to "a failed card stays about a minute; the Conversation section keeps the result".

findings.title: Finished task sessions, which hold the screen text the task read, are kept on disk 10 more minutes for follow-ups that nothing implements
findings.scenario: The consent card says what you ask and what Ember answers is "kept only while it runs". After each task the worker's Copilot session (screen text, tool results) stays in the runtime's store for 10 minutes. After a crash it stays until the next start's sweep. The reason given, "kept for follow-up questions", has no consumer: no code ever resumes a task session.
findings.evidence: tasks.ts:263 `keepMs ?? 10*60_000`; `grep -rn resumeSession app` finds only the conductor (conductor.ts:461); docs/RESEARCH.md:368 describes the resume that was never built; consent copy at app/renderer/home/index.html:34.
findings.fix: Delete the finished session immediately (keepMs 0), or build the follow-up and keep the 10 minutes. At minimum make the consent wording true.

findings.title: start_task's goal is capped at 500 characters while the ask box takes 2000, so long text to be typed cannot reach the worker whole
findings.scenario: The user types a 1,200-character paragraph into the ask box (maxlength 2000) and says "type this into the document". The worker only ever sees the goal string, and the schema rejects goals over 500 characters ("Invalid arguments for start_task…"). The model has to shorten the goal, silently dropping part of the text, or give up. The worker's type_text accepts 5000 characters, so the limit is in the middle of the chain.
findings.evidence: conductor.ts:131 `z.string().min(3).max(500)`; ask box `maxlength="2000"` (app/renderer/ask/index.html:16) and IPC slice(0,2000) (main.ts); the worker's prompt is `Task: ${goal}` (worker.ts:1332) and userWords are not given to it. Schema behaviour read from code, not run live.
findings.fix: Raise the goal cap to about 2000, or pass the user's own words (already in TaskSpec.userWords) to the worker as a separate quoted block.

findings.title: Task results are taken out of the queue before the send, and lost if the send fails
findings.scenario: A task finishes. The user's next question calls takeReports(), which removes the result from the queue, then session.send fails because the runtime just died. Ember reconnects and resumes the conversation, but the finished task's result was in the dropped prompt. When the user asks again, "put it in a new file" has no file name to refer to, and "how did it go?" gets no answer.
findings.evidence: conductor.ts:522 `const reports = this.deps.takeReports?.() ?? []` runs before `await session.send(…)`, and the catch at conductor.ts:536-545 never puts them back. The host's takeReports splice(0)s `carried` and TaskManager.takeReports empties `unreported` (tasks.ts:171).
findings.fix: On a send failure, hand the reports back (a deps.returnReports, or push them onto `carried`) so the next conductor sees them.

findings.title: A successful GitHub sign-in is reported as failed, and the token is lost, if saving the token throws (disk full, read-only data folder)
findings.scenario: The user approves the device code on GitHub. tokens.save(token) (main.ts:993) runs inside the try block and TokenStore.save() does an unguarded fs.writeFileSync (auth.ts:55-57), so ENOSPC, EDQUOT or EACCES makes the whole flow report an error and never calls agent.start(token). The no-keyring case is handled gracefully ('sign-in lasts until Ember quits'); a failed write is not. The same non-atomic writeFileSync can leave a truncated github-token.bin on a crash.
findings.evidence: Code read: main.ts:993-999 and auth.ts save(). Not reproduced end to end (it needs the real device flow).
findings.fix: Wrap save() in try/catch and treat a failed write like 'no keyring': keep the token in memory, connect, and say the sign-in won't survive a restart. Write the token with tmp + rename.

findings.title: Unrecognised Copilot errors are shown raw to the user, and common timeouts are not mapped
findings.scenario: Any error that misses the regexes ("Request timed out after 60000ms", "Cannot read properties of undefined…", "Unexpected token < in JSON…", "Session not found: 7f3c") shows in the bubble, and is spoken aloud when speech is on, as "Copilot reported a problem: <raw text>". No next step is given and it reads as a code error.
findings.evidence: Ran friendlyError on seven plausible raw messages (probe6): every one returns "Copilot reported a problem: <the raw text>". The network regex handles ETIMEDOUT and "fetch failed" but not "timed out" or "timeout".
findings.fix: Add /timed? ?out|timeout|took too long/ → "Copilot took too long to answer. Try again in a moment." For the fallback, say "Copilot reported a problem. Try again; if it keeps happening, check Settings › Copilot." and keep the raw text only in the log.

findings.title: friendlyError leaves common failures as raw text: bare '400' and token-limit errors
findings.scenario: A JSON-bodied 400 ('Error: 400 {…}') shows as 'Copilot reported a problem: 400'. A prompt-too-long error from a long conversation ('prompt token count of N exceeds the limit of M', code model_max_prompt_tokens_exceeded) is not matched by the context rule and shows as 'Copilot reported a problem: CAPIError: 400 prompt token count of 140000 exceeds the limit of 128000'. The user gets technical text and no next step.
findings.evidence: Ran friendlyError on sample strings with the built bundle. 'Error: 400 {…}' gives 'Copilot reported a problem: 400'; 'CAPIError: 400 prompt token count … exceeds the limit' gives the raw text. The context rule at presenter.ts:50 matches only context length/limit/window, 'too long/large' and max tokens. The exact SDK message shapes are from memory of the Copilot API, so confidence is medium-low.
findings.fix: Add /prompt token count|exceeds the limit|token_?limit|max_prompt_tokens/ to the context rule ('This conversation has got too long. Ask me again and I'll start fresh.'). When the stripped message is only a status code, say 'Copilot refused that request (400). Try rephrasing.'

findings.title: With commands off (the default, and for every upgraded user) Ember says it 'doesn't act in terminals' and never mentions Settings › Commands
findings.scenario: An existing user reads the release notes and says 'run df -h'. Ember replies that it doesn't act in terminals and offers to guide them. There is no pointer to Settings › Commands, no 'Open settings' button (WSL has one, and only after the user names WSL), and existing users get no first-run page (L1).
findings.evidence: methodRule(words, false) returns the old 'it doesn't act in terminals' text whenever PromptCaps.commands is false, which is every user until the switch and card. runtime.ts:1048-1054 is the only 'Open settings' offer.
findings.fix: When commands are available but off, let the conductor say 'Commands are off — turn them on in Settings › Commands' and show an 'Open settings' bubble button, once per run.

findings.title: Internal terms leak into user-visible text: "job host", "The worker stopped…", "Node download", "Ember v1", "needs vision", "brain"
findings.scenario: The command tab for a broken Windows or WSL install ends "Couldn't start: Ember's job host is missing, so it can't run commands safely here." (no next step; the other missing-part messages say "Reinstall Ember"). A task that dies without finishing shows "The worker stopped without a summary." on its card, in the notification and in the activity list. A failed SSH set-up says "Ember couldn't check the Node download for build-01…". The Wayland check on the settings page says "Ember v1 needs “GNOME on Xorg”" and the Platform row says "… is not supported in v1", although the app is 0.1.0. The model picker reads "Model for tasks (needs vision)".
findings.evidence: statusLine probe: "Couldn't start: Ember's job host is missing, so it can't run commands safely here." Also local.ts:127 and 781, wsl/discover.ts:136 and wsl/runner.ts:691 ("job host"), worker.ts:1356 ("worker"), ssh-errors.ts:72 ("Node"), environment.ts:137 and 150 ("v1"), index.html:73 ("needs vision"), conductor.ts:517 ("Ember's brain is not connected yet.").
findings.fix: "Part of Ember's install is missing, so it can't run commands safely here. Reinstall Ember."; "The task stopped without saying what happened."; "…couldn't check what it downloaded for build-01 (it doesn't match the expected file)"; "Ember needs “GNOME on Xorg”" and "… isn't supported"; "Model for tasks (must understand images)".
